problems.title: Index-dependent shortest-path ties break edge-bias equivariance
problems.source_location: Section 2.2.2, Eq. (4) and complete-attention invariance statement, PDF pp. 4–5; author modeling/ft_datasets/algos.pyx, floyd_warshall, lines 9–55.
claim: The full graph attention is described as permutation invariant, with edge scores averaged over a selected shortest path.
analysis: Use a diamond graph with paths \(0\to1\to3\) and \(0\to2\to3\), both of length two. Give the first path edge bias zero and the second bias two. The author's Floyd-Warshall implementation updates only on strict distance improvements and processes intermediate indices in order, so it selects the first path. Swapping nodes \(1,2\) and all their attributes while fixing endpoints \(0,3\) switches the chosen bias: \(B_{03}=0\), \(B'_{03}=2\), although equivariance requires \(B'=PBP^\top\) and equality at those fixed endpoints. Distance bias itself remains equivariant; the selected heterogeneous edge bias does not.
result: The unconditional edge-bias equivariance guarantee needs a path-tie condition or invariant aggregation. Unique paths/equal path scores remain unaffected; no checkpoint-specific failure rate or reachability claim is established.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Aggregate shortest-path edge information equivariantly, or state the unique-path/equal-score restriction. This changes the definition and is not a verified trained-model repair.
problems.impact_rationale: A graph relabeling changes the advertised permutation-invariant architecture's heterogeneous edge bias at fixed endpoints. This is a structural counterexample to a core symmetry guarantee, not merely an empirical checkpoint speculation.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
